title: Native ports: games as plain Rust programs

units.title: Design the native port: a game as a plain Rust program
units.detail: june 2026-10-31 (d/modded-builds-are-plain-rust-programs-no-save): a modded build is literally a Rust program: no registers, no GBA memory block, no CPU, nothing preserved for save states or rewind; as regular and pretty as we can make it. Write docs/native-port-design.md covering: (1) where game state lives (globals as typed statics or one Game struct, from DWARF types where a decomp has them; a byte array only where types aren't known yet); (2) the hardware as a library, not memory (the runtime's PPU and sound behind an API like ppu.bg[0].scroll_x, the CPU gone; prior art: the SM64 and OoT PC ports' renderers); (3) the frame loop that replaces the main loop's V-blank wait, and interrupt handlers as callbacks; (4) function pointers as Rust fn values, and as IDs with a lookup table where the game does arithmetic on them (Emerald splits them into halves in task data); (5) ROM addresses as analysis-time facts only: return-address tricks like WarioWare's sub lr, lr, #24 resolved to a fixed destination at lift time (docs/research/code-without-rom-addresses.md); (6) holes: anything not statically resolved (undiscovered code, unresolved indirect jumps, RAM code, untyped pointer arithmetic) is a build error or a listed hole, since there's no interpreter fallback; (7) the oracle: the native program draws the same frames as the play build from the same inputs (the play build and its exact checks become the native port's oracle); (8) data pointers, DMA and struct copies, and what each needs. Read the existing analysis, structured codegen and mod-view designs first; cite the code. Propose the units that follow. Stop at ~3 h.

record.evidence: docs/native-port-design.md covers the card's 8 points with code citations and proposes 8 units (5 new filed). A fresh-context verifier spot-checked 20 citations, the WarioWare arithmetic and the units: first FAIL (Ref over non-POD Game, BIOS copy timing, 8 lesser points), all fixed, recheck PASS. just check passes after merging main.

units.title: Spike: one of our agb programs as a native Rust program
units.detail: Take one of our own agb programs (agb/, our own source: small, no legal issues; one with a frame loop, input and a background or sprites, e.g. agb/template or agb/windows-blend) and lift it all the way to a native Rust program per docs/native-port-design.md: no Machine, no registers, no GBA memory map; state in Rust types, the hardware through the library API, a frame loop. Done when it draws the same frames as its play build (exact recompiled build) for the same input script over a few hundred frames, the code is committed, and the doc records what was hard, what was done by hand that the lifter should do, and what the next units should be. Stop at ~4 h with what's measured. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): no agb/ program reads input, so first write a new agb/native-spike (agb source only; D-pad moves a sprite and scrolls a background; SCENE.md). The native program lives in its own crate (crates/native-spike or agb/native-spike-native, your call) and takes the desktop's flags: --headless --frames N --input <script> --frame-hashes F. Done when: native and the exact play build give identical --frame-hashes files over 600 frames of a script that moves something at least every 60 frames, and one planted wrong store makes them differ.

record.evidence: just native-spike: native = play, 600 frames identical (510 distinct pictures), hashes file 5539f4ec2af9bb48, last frame 600 hash e40446740c70e154; planted wrong store (plant feature, OAM attr1 x+1 while facing left) caught at frame 212 (play f6dee7bb5c6ee4b7, planted f60d58b8ffc489bf). Script holds a D-pad key in every 60 frames (longest gap 10). Verifier reran agb-tests + native-spike and cmp'd its own runs: identical, planted differs frames 212-541. Findings: docs/research/native-agb-spike.md. Branch t3/a5d53ea7, unmerged.

notes.text: Per docs/native-port-design.md: make the spike's hardware library a throwaway adapter over today's Bus; the real one is {unit:native/hw-library}. The exact play build is a fine oracle for a lag-free program; timers or lag frames wait on q/may-native-port-s-check.

units.title: Hole report: what blocks a native build of each game
units.detail: A tool (Rust, not bash) that lists, for a ROM, everything that blocks a pure native build per docs/native-port-design.md's hole list: code reached in runs or fuzzing that discovery didn't find; indirect jumps and calls not resolved; return-address arithmetic (the scrambled-return-address side-by-side tool from docs/research/code-without-rom-addresses.md finds it, e.g. WarioWare's IWRAM helper); code run from RAM; pointer arithmetic or casts the known types don't explain, where types exist. Run it on the eight games of that research (Emerald, Kirby, Metroid Zero Mission, Minish Cap, WarioWare, moonbeam and the rest) and write each game's counts and worst holes into docs/research/native-holes.md, ranked by how close each game is to native. Propose discovery or fuzzing units aimed at the commonest holes. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): put the hard-hole classification in the analysis crate (the lifter reuses it). Runs: the research doc's 5,400-frame press script through the interpreter's coverage, for all eight ROMs listed by file name. Untyped pointer arithmetic: report 'not measured until stage B'. Rank by hard holes, then bytes reached but not discovered. Done when native-holes.md's counts match the tool's output on all eight, and the controls hold: WarioWare's 0x3000468 lr-24 helper listed as a hole, moonbeam's __gnu_thumb1_case_* resolved, Emerald's unresolved-jump count equals Recovery's.

record.evidence: just holes on all eight ROMs (5,400 frames, research press script): each first line identical to docs/research/native-holes.md's ranking lines (Metroid 18, WarioWare 22, moonbeam 23, Kirby AM 29, Kirby NiDL 30, Emerald 34, Minish Cap 46, Rogue 86). Controls: WarioWare 0x03000468 site-24 listed NOT resolved; moonbeam __gnu_thumb1_case_uqi/uhi (0x08042e00/14) resolved; Emerald 11 unresolved = Recovery's 670-659 (just discover). Classification in analysis::holes, cargo test -p analysis holes 10 passed. Review: fresh subagent, 11 findings fixed or documented (b251fd00). just check, disc-pret, disc-agb, jt-score pass.

units.title: Emerald: ten functions as native Rust, scored against pret
units.detail: Like {unit:mod/decomp-spike}, but native per docs/native-port-design.md: ten Emerald functions of varied shape (a leaf getter, an array loop, a call chain, a switch, struct field access, u8/u16 arithmetic, one that stores a function pointer; ClearBattleMonForms and SeedRngAndSetTrainerId among them) lifted to plain Rust over typed state from pret's DWARF, with no registers, Machine or addresses. Emerald is the measuring stick, not the goal: score each against pret's C (statements, named accesses, loop shapes, anything left raw), and say what the lifter needs for each gap. Check behaviour where it can be: the same results as the play build's function on the same inputs (fn-diff style). Write side-by-sides and scores into docs/native-port-design.md. Never copy pret's C text into the repo ({d:mod-view-prints-pret-s-file-line-never-pret-s-c}). Stop at ~3 h. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): mirror-safe (decision): lifted code and side-by-sides go in mods/emerald/native-ten/ (left out of the public mirror); docs/native-port-design.md gets only scores and gaps. The ten: {unit:mod/decomp-spike}'s eight (mods/emerald/decomp-spike/) plus CalcCRC16 and GetBgAttribute; reuse its scoring columns. Behaviour check: a native form of fn-diff (entry state as guest-layout RAM + params from {unit:native/summaries}; compare RAM, I/O, return value, ignoring stack below sp). Done when it prints 'native 0 of 10 differ' and a one-byte edit gets caught.

record.evidence: just native-ten: 'native 0 of 10 differ' (3,072 runs), ROM-byte fault under Random caught 671/672; verifier's own one-byte edits (CalcCRC16 0x8408->0x8409, GetBgType arm) caught; 19 hand edits caught. Review by fresh subagent: 6 findings fixed (8372fdfe). just check passes.

units.title: The GBA hardware as a library both builds share
units.detail: docs/native-port-design.md section 2: split Video (display registers decoded, VRAM, palette, OAM) and Audio out of runtime::Bus; the PPU and mixer take them; Hw with typed registers (ppu.bg[n].scroll_x), the BIOS routines over slices, wait_vblank/idle/beam reads (section 3), DMA kinds (section 8). no_std. Done when the play build's checks are unchanged (first-frame, routes' frame hashes, same-states with --timing exact) and Hw has unit tests drawing a frame from fields alone. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): 'unchanged' means against the play binary built from main before your change. Done when: just unit passes for every units/*.toml; route-check --same-states <pre-change emerald bin> <post-change bin> --every 60 units/emerald-newgame.toml shows 0 differences; just gba-tests, just armwrestler, just mgba-oracle and just check pass; a cargo test -p runtime test setting only Hw fields reproduces every pixel in agb/template/SCENE.md. Existing Emerald save states must still load (snap's versioned-layout test); if the payload must change, bump the version and keep loading the old one.

record.evidence: runtime tests 266/266 incl. template_scene_from_fields_alone (every pixel of agb/template/SCENE.md from Hw fields alone); check-nostd ok; route-check --same-states main-built Emerald vs new, emerald-newgame --every 60: 93 frames same, 0 diffs; gba-tests, armwrestler, mgba-oracle, just check pass; native-spike on new Hw, hashes 5539f4ec2af9bb48; save payload unchanged. just unit 14/19: the 5 misses fail byte-identically on main before the change (filed as {unit:oracle/five-routes-red-on-main}). Sound, timers, serial, saves not split out yet.

notes.text: Built on t3/native-hw-library; all checks pass but 5 units (affine, mosaic-modes, windows-blend: compiled share under min_compiled; armwrestler-fixed/original: recompiled parts from interp) fail identically on main before the change: same hashes. Not marked done; overseer's call.

units.title: Function summaries: parameters, results, callee-saves
units.detail: docs/native-port-design.md section 5: Van Emmerik-style bottom-up summaries over the call graph (registers-and-types.md): r0-r3 read on entry, registers defined on every return that callers read, r4-r11 and sp proven preserved; failures listed. Done when Emerald's summaries agree with pret's DWARF prototypes on a stated share, every disagreement explained, and the counts are in the design doc. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): extend codegen::saves (gbaa-recompile --saves already proves callee-saves for 8,894 of 15,158 Emerald functions), don't start over. Agree means summary params ⊆ DWARF prototype params and return matches (pret DWARF via crates/pret-names/src/dwarf.rs / names/pokeemerald.toml proto; readelf can't read it). No bar (decision: measure only): the tool prints agree/disagree/no-proto counts and per-category disagreement counts, 10 per category checked by hand, numbers quoted in the design doc. A unit test where a function clobbers r4 fails its proof.

record.evidence: gbaa-recompile --summaries on Emerald (codegen::saves::summarize/compare, extends the callee-save proof): 13,359 agree, 1,664 disagree, 133 no proto, 2 unreadable (694 disagree trusting indirect calls); categories 1/505/656/0/0/619/0/1, all traced to 4 roots in docs/native-port-design.md s5; --saves still 8,894/15,158; r4-clobber test passes; just check, first-frame x4, gba-tests, mgba-oracle pass; review fixed; verifier re-ran and hand-checked.

units.title: Play build timing that matches a native program
units.detail: docs/native-port-design.md section 7, option 1, if june picks it: --timing native for gbaa-recompile and the interpreter: blocks cost nothing; the clock moves only at BIOS waits, at store-free call-free loop back edges (a list from analysis, shared with the native lifter) and at VCOUNT/DISPSTAT/timer-counter reads, by the library's steps. Done when compiled matches interpreted under it (first-frame style) on the agb programs and Emerald's new-game route frames. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): june chose this (d/may-native-port-s-check, option a); ignore 'if june picks it'. Include section 7's BIOS copy/fill/decompress and DMA costs (bios::call pricing) so Emerald's VRAM fill still spans a V-blank. route-check and recompile-check hard-code --timing exact: give them a timing parameter. Compare states, not mGBA hashes. Done when: just first-frame <rom> 60 native (or equivalent) passes for every program in $GBAA_DATA/agb; route-check --timing native --same-states compiled vs --interp --every 60 units/emerald-newgame.toml shows 0 differences; unit tests: N plain instructions move the clock 0, a VCOUNT poll loop exits after exactly the right lines, a 96 KB CpuFastSet crosses a V-blank.

record.evidence: verifier-9f1849: unit tests ok (no-time, VCOUNT poll 201 reads to line 100, 96 KB CpuFastSet crosses V-blank, spin budget then half lines; hw::spin same); just check exit 0; first-frame 60 native 15/15 identical (re-ran 3); Emerald native compiled vs --interp 93 frames 0 diffs, past CB2_NewGame to the truck at 5400; Emerald exact vs main-built base 93 frames 0 diffs, generated exact code unchanged. Reviews: 2 fresh-subagent rounds, fixes in f773f153, 1bb455af.

notes.text: Next units: hw::spin moves exactly half a line past budget; the play build runs to the next event (a timer's can come first). Store-and-poll loops with no call need crates/runtime/spins.toml (Emerald's librfu at 0x082e2b6a); the hole report only finds call loops.

Hole report measured busy loops that call functions (64+ non-progressing iterations in a row, reading IRQ-written RAM): only Emerald Rogue, 3 (LoadMapInStepsLocal, FreeTempTileDataBuffersIfPossible, CB2_NewGame). The 90 s route doesn't reach Emerald's map load.

Branch t3/c58bf1ab f773f153: --timing native built (runtime, codegen, idle list in analysis, route-check --timing, first-frame TIMING). Emerald native hangs after frame 5040: DoMapLoadLoop polls via calls (no idle edge), so no time passes. Needs a rule; see report.

units.title: Stage-A lifter: a whole program as Rust over byte RAM
units.detail: docs/native-port-design.md sections 1-6, stage A: print a whole program from IR, structuring plan and summaries as plain Rust: no registers, CPU, stack or cycles; RAM as byte regions in Game; I/O through Hw; FnRef IDs; holes.toml for stand-ins, hard holes fail the build. Done when the agb spike's program lifts with no hand edits and passes the native check against its play build. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): runs last, after {unit:native/oracle} and {unit:native/timing-native}. Against overfitting, also lift a second agb program the spike didn't touch (agb/affine or mosaic-modes). Done when, with no hand edits, the lifter's output for the spike program and the second program builds and passes the native check (route-check --native) against the --timing native play build for 600 frames, and a planted hard hole fails the build, named. ADDED 2026-11-01 from {unit:native/oracle}: build --fn-ids rom (FnRef IDs as ROM addresses in the check build) and run the native check with no replaced-library skip list (a literal lift keeps agb's RAM and VRAM state, so all RAM outside stack and code copies is compared). Lifted BIOS copies call hw::spend(cpu_set_cycles(...)); idle edges get hw::idle, spin edges hw::spin, per runtime::spins.

record.evidence: just lift-check (verifier-7c3e reran it, exit 0): gbaa-lift's output for agb/native-spike, agb/affine and agb/mosaic-modes, no hand edits (regenerated identical), passes route-check --native against the --timing native play build for 600 frames each with no --replaced list ('pass (600 frames, 0 differences in pictures, RAM, I/O, palette, VRAM and OAM)'); planted wrong store caught (frame 2: EWRAM byte 0x020000c0); planted hard hole fails lift and build ('error: hard hole in f_03000000 at 0x03000034: CPU state: mrs'). FnRefs are ROM keys; CpuSet spends cpu_set_cycles; hw::idle/hw::spin at the play build's edges. 0 hard holes, 4 holes-file stand-ins per program. just check, just native-check, gba-tests, disc-agb, disc-pret, jt-score, mgba-oracle, first-frame all pass. Review by a fresh subagent: 7 points, the real ones fixed (I/O offsets past 0x3FF, unused I/O halfwords, CpuSet bound, call returning into another entry, stale-output trap, name case, orphan stand-ins).

notes.text: Done on branch t3/e2c662e5. Stage B: agb is 109 of 111 functions; stack frames are IWRAM bytes (sp a parameter); fallthrough into another entry is a tail call losing r4-r11; Game::cpsr's I bit doesn't hold IRQs at waits. Discovery gaps decoded at lift (mosaic 143).

units.title: Native check: frames and RAM against the play build
units.detail: docs/native-port-design.md section 7: --layout guest and --fn-ids rom build parameters for a native program, and a route-check mode running a native binary and the play build on the same presses, comparing every frame, EWRAM/IWRAM outside the guest stack, Video and audio per frame, and naming the first difference. Plus the check that guest and packed layouts draw the same frames. Done on the agb spike's program. HARDENED (sprint 2026-10-31): runs after timing-native and before lift-stage-a, on the spike's hand-written native program (the spike provides both layouts by hand if needed); compares against the --timing native play build. The play build must report the lowest sp reached (new). Add a sound program (bios-sound or psg-square) besides the spike. Done when route-check --native NATIVE_BIN PLAY_BIN ROUTE reports 0 differences in frames, RAM outside stack and copy destinations, Video and audio for both, and names the frame and byte of a planted one-store fault; guest and packed layouts give identical --frame-hashes. AMENDED by the overseer 2026-11-01 after verifier-a7c3: audio samples move to {unit:native/hw-sound} (the library has no mixer; registers and wave RAM are compared); --fn-ids rom moves to {unit:native/lift-stage-a} (the spike has no function references); RAM skips for agb state the hand-written native programs replace are accepted, listed in crates/native-spike/check/*.replaced.toml and printed every run, and the lifter's literal lift must compare with no skip list.

record.evidence: just native-check: native-spike 600 frames 0 differences in pictures, RAM, I/O, palette, VRAM, OAM; play layout = guest layout; planted store caught (frame 212, OAM 0x07000002). psg-square 120 frames 0 differences, sound registers and wave RAM compared, samples not (no mixer: moved to {unit:native/hw-sound}). gba-tests, mgba-oracle, first-frame, native-spike, just check pass. verifier-a7c3 confirmed all compared clauses; its three misses were split by the overseer: audio samples to {unit:native/hw-sound}, --fn-ids rom to {unit:native/lift-stage-a}, replaced-agb RAM skips accepted (listed, printed every run).

notes.text: Built: route-check --native (just native-check), 0 diffs on spike+psg-square in what's compared. Verifier-a7c3 FAIL: psg-square audio not compared (no mixer in hw, --no-audio), agb RAM/VRAM skipped as replaced, no --fn-ids rom. Branch t3/42ef8378.

units.title: Discovery takes the run's call targets as function starts
units.detail: From {unit:native/hole-report} (docs/research/native-holes.md): the largest hard hole in five of the eight games is a call through a register to an address discovery doesn't know as a start (13-26 a game in seven of the eight; e.g. Emerald's m4a SoundMainBTM family called from 0x082dfb5a). Make those starts: a per-game roots list from gbaa-holes' Run::indirect_calls/call_targets, or find the tables statically. Done when `just holes` shows 0 calls to non-entries in ROM on the eight, and disc-pret, disc-agb and jt-score keep their bars.

record.evidence: Fresh verifier subagent, merged branch: just holes on all eight lists 0 ROM targets among calls to non-entries (left: Metroid 4, WarioWare 2, Minish 1, all RAM). disc-pret 0.9991/0.9549, disc-agb 1.0/0.9835 and 1.0/0.5789, jt-score 676/676 and 584/617, far 548/548 and 726/732: all exit 0. just check passes.

notes.text: Roots come from the holes run itself (discover_with, in-process): only targets the press script reaches. The lifter doesn't take run roots yet; a native game build needs a roots source. New m4a code shows bx r12 returns: {unit:native/recovery-saved-lr-return}.

units.title: Discovery finds code games copy to RAM themselves
units.detail: From {unit:native/hole-report}: every game but moonbeam runs RAM code no overlay discovered (300-2,908 bytes: WarioWare's IWRAM loop from ROM 0x080007e4, Emerald's SoundMainRAM and IntrMain, Metroid's 0x03003b90/0x03004100, Minish Cap's 0x030040e0). Overlays only take BIOS CpuSet/CpuFastSet with constant args. Find copy loops and CpuSet with arguments discovery can't fold yet (or take the run's RamRun::rom_src as copies). Done when `just holes` shows 0 RAM bytes undiscovered outside the flash stack routines on the eight, and disc-pret, disc-agb, jt-score keep their bars.

record.evidence: Review fix made (5385f735): ram_copies skips groups at mirror addresses, unit test covers 0x0300_8100 and 0x0204_0100. Merged main (5385f735), just check passes. Fresh verifier ran just holes on all eight: 0 RAM bytes undiscovered each; disc-pret 0.9991/0.9549, disc-agb 1.0/0.9835 and 1.0/0.5789, jt-score 676/676, 548/548, 584/617, 726/732, all at their bars.

notes.text: The loop's review asked for fixes before landing (all on the card): - crates/analysis/src/holes/copies.rs:130-138 (`ram_copies`, the found-copies loop): `region_end` is 0x0204_0000 for EWRAM and 0x0300_8000 for anything else, but `exec` takes all RAM code in 0x0200_0000..0x0400_…
Copies come from the run (analysis::holes::ram_copies), not static: a lift with no run still lacks them. A static finder (DMA3 stores, copy loops) would be its own unit.

units.title: Coverage past the press script reaches the unresolved jumps
units.detail: From {unit:native/hole-report}: of 109 unresolved indirect jumps over the eight games only 14 ran in the 5,400-frame press script (Rogue 2 of 50, Minish Cap 5 of 25). Feed gbaa-fuzz (or longer routes/save states) into gbaa-holes' Run so each unresolved jump is either seen with targets (a holes.toml list the coverage runs check) or shown unreached by everything. Done when native-holes.md has, per game, reached-by-any-run counts and each reached jump's observed targets.

record.evidence: Fresh verifier subagent: native-holes.md 'Coverage runs' per-game counts (88 of 165 unresolved jumps reached by any run, 68 by press script) match holes/coverage/*.toml jump lists; each reached jump's targets listed; WarioWare and Minish Cap reruns of gbaa-holes --cover in check mode matched their lists (exit 0); just check passed after merging main.

units.title: Hardware library stand-in for the flash save stack routines
units.detail: From {unit:native/hole-report}: five of the eight games (Emerald, both Kirbys, Metroid, Emerald Rogue) copy the agb flash library's routines (ReadFlash_Core and siblings) onto the IWRAM stack at 0x03007dxx and run them; the bytes change between copies, a hard hole each time. One stand-in in the native hardware library (flash reads/writes as library calls), recognised at the copy, covers all five. Done when `just holes` counts 0 changed RAM runs at 0x03007dxx on those five.

record.evidence: Fresh verifier subagent ran just holes on Emerald, both Kirbys, Metroid, Rogue: 0 changed RAM runs at 0x03007dxx in each (Rogue's one left is its mixer at 0x030059f0); hard totals 29/21/25/7/80, were 34/29/30/18/86. ReadFlash1/ReadFlash_Core/VerifyFlashSector_Core recognised by analysis::flash, stood in by runtime::hw::flash, checked against agb_flash.c. just check passes after merging main; lift-check --only native-spike passes (Hw gained save).

notes.text: Not wired into gbaa-lift yet (no lifted game saves to flash): at a recognised call into RAM, call Routine::call on Hw::save. Hw::save starts as Flash512; a program must set its kind. Exemption is by address only (see holes.rs doc).

units.title: Sound in the hardware library: mixer, timers, FIFOs
units.detail: Split out of {unit:native/oracle} (2026-11-01): runtime::hw has no mixer, so the native check compares sound registers and wave RAM but not samples, and timers, FIFOs and DMA sound aren't modelled. Split Audio out of runtime::Bus (docs/native-port-design.md section 2), give Hw the play build's mixer, timers and DMA-to-FIFO, so the play build and native programs share one sound path. Done when route-check --native on units/psg-square.toml passes without --no-audio (samples equal every frame), a native bios-sound (direct sound via timer+DMA) passes the same, the play build's audio checks (docs/tools/commands.md audio-*) are unchanged, and just check passes.

record.evidence: Verifier reran just native-check: psg-square passes 120 frames with audio the same in 120 frames, no --no-audio, planted wrong sample caught at frame 74 on audio; direct-sound (stands for bios-sound, decision recorded) passes 300 frames with audio the same in all; native-spike still passes. just psg-square and psg-wave-noise match mGBA. Main session also: mgba-audio-diff byte-identical on the 18157 Hz ROM (600) and 10512 Hz ROM (1000), audio-check on both, audio-pace, lift-check pass; just check passes after merging main.

notes.text: Not yet in hw: H-blank DMA's price on the clock, DMA/FIFO DMA by address via write16 (panics). direct-sound has no planted fault; psg-square's plant covers the audio compare.

units.title: Lift report metrics and a bars file the lift check holds
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md, 'How every piece is checked' and piece 0. Shared code every stage-B unit needs. (1) gbaa-lift writes its metrics into report.txt as `name value` lines, split by region so later bars mean something: lines of src/main.rs; functions lifted, recognised, replaced, unrecognised; functions with a summary hole; four-register functions without a summary hole; byte loads/stores at a constant address per region (RAM, I/O, ROM, VRAM/palette/OAM); at a computed address per region where the value set says, else unknown; sp-relative loads/stores; call_fn calls; jumps by value; stand-ins; gap targets (codegen::native's count() today lumps these). (2) `--bars FILE` fails the lift when any metric is over its bar (maxima only; a unit that needs a relation adds a metric whose bar is 0), naming it. (3) The program list moves out of the lift-check recipe into the same committed TOML (one table per program: ROM, route, flags, bars) read by a Rust driver (a gbaa-lift or route-check mode), so later units add a program by adding a table, not bash ({d:stage-b-checks-are-bars-in-one-committed-file}). Bars start at today's values; only lowered. Done when: just lift-check runs from the TOML and passes; a codegen test lowers one bar below the measured value and the lift fails naming that metric; the planted store and planted hard hole are still caught; just check passes.

record.evidence: just lift-check from crates/codegen/lift-check.toml (gbaa-lift-check driver): every metric within its bar for affine, mosaic-modes, native-spike; three routes pass (600 frames, 0 differences); planted store caught (frame 2 EWRAM 0x020000c0); planted hard hole caught (f_03000000 mrs). tests/lift_bars.rs: load_computed_unknown bar lowered to 0 fails the lift 'load_computed_unknown is 755, over its bar of 0', only that bar. Driver with load_sp 2232->2231 fails before builds naming it. just check exit 0; disc-agb and jt-score exit 0. Fresh reviewer subagent passed all four items; its 3 minor points fixed.

units.title: Fallthrough into another function keeps r4-r11 and flags
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md, piece 1. Stage A prints a fall (or jump) into another function's entry as a tail call, so the continuation starts with r4-r11 and NZCV zeroed (codegen::native goto/call_then). Real agbcc games do this. Give the continuation the caller's registers and flags: an extended entry taking them, or the continuation's blocks copied into the caller (your call; say why in docs/native-stage-b.md). Write a new agb program of ours, agb/native-fallthrough (source only, SCENE.md, a units/*-600.toml route; global_asm! units.title: IRQs held while CPSR's I bit is set
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md, piece 1. Game::cpsr is bookkeeping in stage A: an IRQ due at a wait (hw::wait_*, idle, spin) inside a critical section runs at once; the hardware holds it until a CPSR write clears I, and the play build does what the hardware does. Make waits wake without dispatching while I is set, and a CPSR write that clears I (the critical-section restore stand-ins, msr) dispatch what's pending. Reach: runtime::hw's dispatch can't see Game::cpsr today, so the Native trait gains a way to ask (update crates/native-spike's two impls, mods/emerald/native-ten/ram.rs and runtime tests); wait_irq loops until a handler runs, so with I set it must return on wake instead of hanging. Write a new agb program of ours, agb/native-irq-hold (source only, SCENE.md, a units/*-600.toml route): a V-blank handler that counts frames, and a critical section around a VCOUNT poll loop past line 160 whose result depends on whether the handler ran inside it. Add it to just lift-check with its bars; keep the old behaviour behind a gbaa-lift flag. Done when: just lift-check passes with the new program; lifted with the old-behaviour flag it fails the native check; a runtime unit test covers wake-without-dispatch and wait_irq with I set returning; just check passes.

units.title: A pending IRQ is taken the moment IME is set again
units.detail: Found by {unit:native/lift-irq-hold}, written up in docs/native-stage-b.md. agb's critical_section, and agbcc games, mask by clearing IME rather than the I bit; on the hardware a pending IRQ is taken the moment IME is written back to 1. Both the play build at --timing native and the hardware library take it at the next wait instead. They agree with each other, so the native check can't see it; only mGBA can. Write a small agb test program (source only, like agb/native-irq-hold) that clears IME across V-blank and reads its frame count before and after setting IME again; fix the hardware library and tick_native so an IME write releases held IRQs, like hw::irq_release for the I bit. Keep the old behaviour behind a gbaa-lift flag as a planted_flags control. Done when: the test program's route matches mGBA's hash (just mgba-diff) on both the play build at --timing native and the exact interpreter; just lift-check passes with the program added and the flag's control caught; just check passes.

units.title: Function flow: the heap by allocation site and field
units.detail: Behind its own switch, GBAA_FNREF_HEAP, off by default (the function-flow thread's method, 2026-11-19: off, the flow is exactly main's). On, it turns the RAM-pointer rules on too, which it rests on. The rule (crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs, 'The heap by allocation site'): a direct call of a function the holes file names as an allocator (allocators = [0x...]) returns a pointer to an object of its own, by call site; a store through it at a known offset goes to that site's cell for that word, through an unknown index to the site's any-cell; a load reads its word's cell, the any-cell and the pile, and no global's cell. A pointer below the one returned is the allocator's header, the heap's RAM. Judged on C programs and games ({unit:native/c-bars}): c/heap (agbcc and modern GCC, in crates/codegen/lift-check.toml), and Emerald's flow with pret's allocators named. Done when: with GBAA_FNREF_HEAP and GBAA_FNREF_LIVE on, fn_words_not_proven on c-heap is lower than with GBAA_FNREF_RAM and GBAA_FNREF_LIVE on (both values in the evidence; the heap switch alone doesn't move it: say so), no C or agb bar over with the switches off, unit tests for two heap objects kept apart and two fields of one kept apart, Emerald's time and peak with the switch on measured, just check passes. It turns on by default with the RAM pointers ({unit:native/fnref-ram-default}); until then it is off.

record.evidence: On main at 1d72731e (the tested tree; just check exit 0; lift-metrics 0 over, 0 under with the switches off). The rule is behind GBAA_FNREF_HEAP, off (crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs, 'The heap by allocation site'; c/heap, agbcc and modern GCC, in the lift check, names its allocators in holes/c-heap-*.toml). fn_words_not_proven on c-heap-agbcc and c-heap-gcc: 0 each with GBAA_FNREF_HEAP and GBAA_FNREF_LIVE on (8 of 8 proven, 4 of 4 call sets complete), 6 each with GBAA_FNREF_RAM and GBAA_FNREF_LIVE, 7 each off; the heap switch alone doesn't move it (7, as the RAM switch alone): the gain needs the registers' rules and the names' objects ({unit:native/fnref-ram-anchors}). Emerald with the heap and registers' switches and pret's Alloc and AllocZeroed named: settles in 26 rounds, 1,385 s, 0.95 GB (1,329 s with RAM and registers, 557 s off). Unit tests: two allocations apart, two fields of one apart, an index, the header, a sub back to the start, a wrapper allocator, any-allocation reads, many sites; 93 pass. Two fresh-subagent reviews of the diffs (a Thumb sub on an allocation's pointer, masks, kept ops, wrappers fixed); the independent checker ran the tests and the c-heap tables for each switch combination and read the gating: PASS, noting the gain needs GBAA_FNREF_LIVE. It turns on with the RAM pointers ({unit:native/fnref-ram-default}).

units.title: Function flow: callees' values kept apart by call site
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md piece 3. Measured by {unit:native/fnref-heap-sites} (its branch, commit 35356cf4, splits the pile into frame and allocation-site objects): fn_words_not_proven doesn't move on any agb program, even with the pile dropped altogether. The run joins every caller's r0-r3 and sp at a callee's entry, and every call_fn set is all ~21 address-taken functions, so a shared function's pointer parameters (memcpy, fmt, qrcodegen's encoders) reach dozens of frames, anywhere in each, and one read through them gives every function address stored in any. units.title: Stand-ins for libgcc's double multiply and divide
units.detail: libgcc's ieee754-df.S __muldf3 and __divdf3 call their denormal paths (Lml_s, Ldv_s) by bleq, which return r4/r5 changed: a real register-convention break, hard holes in moonbeam (6) and Emerald Rogue (3) after {unit:native/callee-save-breaks} (docs/research/native-holes.md, 'Functions that change r4-r11 or sp'). Write each as a stand-in (Rust f64 mul/div, bit-exact on the soft-float's results), found by its code the way analysis::flash recognises routines, so every game with them gets it. Done when: gbaa-holes counts none of them hard on moonbeam and Rogue (the report must learn the stand-ins), a test pins the f64 results against the interpreter on edge cases (denormals, NaN, inf, rounding), just check passes.

Verifier read NaN/inf/zero rules against the disassembly: match. just check passes after merging main.

units.title: Tell masked entry reads of r4-r11 from parameters
units.detail: After {unit:native/callee-save-breaks}, a function that keeps r4-r11 and reads one as it came is soft ('reads r4-r11 at entry and keeps them'): mostly agbcc building a word byte by byte in an unset register, every old bit masked away, but TMC's sub_080086D8 takes r8/r11 from player.s as parameters (Minish 0x08060ba1 derefs entry r5 too), which the lift gets wrong (Regs::call zeroes r4-r12). Track which bits of an entry value survive (and/orr masks, uses as address or callee argument, hi-reg mov then pass-on); make a surviving read hard. Done when: the soft kind holds only fully-masked reads (doc lists the corpus's), holes-all --against shows the new hard ones named, just check passes.

record.evidence: Verifier (fresh context) PASS: just check exit 0 after merging main; holes-all --against out/holes/2359ecdd-dirty (out/holes/tailcall) names 36 hard entry-read functions, matching the doc's table; soft kinds hold only fully-masked reads and only-jumped ones (Rogue 15, Nightmare 1, moonbeam 1). Review fix: tail calls/falls from called functions count as calls, with a test.

notes.text: No test covers the falls edge (saves.rs sum.falls) or a chain of jumps through the fixpoint; tail-call edge is tested. A fall after the jumper changed r4-r11 is labelled hard (over-hard, safe).

The loop's review asked for fixes before landing (all on the card): - crates/codegen/src/saves/summary.rs:733-777 and :919-952 (the `bl` map and the `readers.difference(&called)` relabel to `JUMPED_READ`): tail calls are left out on purpose (`.filter_map(|(&at, &c)| c.filter(|&c…

Rules settled by corpus reruns: a merge of entry bits with anything else is unknown (else LLVM paths go hard); returned entry bits count only if a caller's own instruction reads them (agbcc pop {r3}; mov r8, r3). 7 of the 36 hard not looked into (doc).

units.title: Function flow: loads through unknown addresses
units.detail: docs/native-stage-b.md piece 3. Measured on {unit:native/fnref-context}'s branch (commit 4ff476a; it holds the object split and call-site context): fn_words_not_proven unmoved by either. ~640 of affine's load sites (spike 644) have an address that may be unknown (Val::unk), and each reads the pile and every RAM cell (Run::load_at's anywhere arm), so e.g. the IRQ vector word's f_03000000 is in nearly every hole. Not the cause (tried, no change): naming the allocator, dropping the pile from constant-address loads, dropping the I/O unk flag, NUMS 8->256. A seen source: main's inlined free-list walk at 0x080001a8 (affine) loads GLOBAL_ALLOC fields holding allocator-made pointers. Find where the unknown comes from (GBAA_FNREF_TRACE; print each anywhere load) and fix the first big source. units.title: Ref<T> objects in static arrays fit the packed layout
units.detail: Found by {unit:native/lift-bios-calls}: heap.rs makes an object where a RAM base meets an unknown index, so an element of a static array (agb/native-bios-calls 2018f08's OUT.regs[k], 16 bytes at 0x020000b8) prints as g.at(Ref::<H_..>). The same words are also constant-address globals, which --layout packed places apart (in the lifter's order), so Ram::span fails and the packed build panics: 'pointer 0x020000b8 to 16 bytes isn't in RAM in one piece'. The guest layout passes. Repro: build agb/native-bios-calls at 2018f08 (its main loop colours from o.regs.iter()) and run just lift-check --only native-bios-calls. The program now colours from a returned copy to avoid it; any game indexing a static array its code also touches by constant address hits it. Fix in the lifter (keep such globals contiguous in packed, or leave objects whose base is a global's region as bytes). Done when: the 2018f08 loop shape (as a lift-check program or test) passes the packed native check; lift-check and just check pass.

record.evidence: Verifier subagent aa82f59c: lift-check --only native-bios-calls passed with the 2018f08 loop (o.regs.iter()) restored: 600 frames, packed layout draws the same; just check passed. units.title: Flow's ROM from-here-on widening keeps pointers it reads
units.detail: Val::cap lets RomFrom(lo) absorb Rom(a) for any a >= lo, but rom_from(lo) reads only up to the next code, so a pointer past it is never read and a call through it may get a complete callee set missing callees. Seen in mosaic-modes (found by {unit:native/fnref-flow-emerald}): fn 0x080037f1 (core::fmt pad) r0 widens to RomFrom(0x08000100), absorbing vtable Rom(0x08024c50); word 0x08024c5c (f_08002ee1) was read only transiently before. Make the widening keep such pointers (mark lost_rom, or don't absorb past bound) with a unit test; just lift-metrics bars hold (lower any that drop).

record.evidence: Val::cap absorbs into RomFrom(lo) only pointers before the next code (run-scoped code-address list), ROMS widening per data run; 2 unit tests fail on old code, 24 fnref tests pass. Merged main (a9e163f): just lift-metrics 0 over/0 under at main's bars (owner's raise already covered), just check green.

units.title: The lifter handles reset and IRQ-wrapper msr/mrs itself
units.detail: From the overnight lift (2026-11-11, runs/long/overnight-lift.log): every one of the seven games that failed to lift has 2-5 msr/mrs hard holes, nearly all in the reset code at 0x08000000 and the IRQ wrapper. analysis::holes::classify already returns these as CpuWhere::Boot and CpuWhere::Wrapper (recognised, not holes; docs/research/native-holes.md, What the Stage-A lifter should know), but the lifter still makes them hard, and Metroid and Kirby Nightmare get past them only by hand stand-ins in mods/<game>/holes.toml. Have the lifter print the reset's mode switches and stack setup as the program's start and the IRQ wrapper's PSR saves as runtime::hw IRQ entry/exit (keep The native-timing play build takes an IRQ the I bit held as soon as an msr clears I), so no game needs these stand-ins; msr/mrs anywhere else stay hard. units.title: Function flow passes only registers a callee reads
units.detail: docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'Registers nobody reads' and 'A C game', follow-up 2. The function flow (crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs) takes back all of r0-r3 after a call as the callee's returns hold them, set or not, so a register a callee never writes comes back as every caller's value of it joined: a handler called through r0 that returns nothing returns its own address, and a call with an empty callee set takes those back from every address-taken function (on Metroid 77 words at 0x0800535a and 13 at 0x08001416; on Emerald 1,373 at 0x0801d874). Rule: a register a callee leaves as it came on every return (its summary's exit bits, codegen::saves, where the summary's run and its callees' didn't stop at a hole) keeps the caller's own value after the call, as the lifted program has it (a shaped callee doesn't return it). Lands behind its own switch, GBAA_FNREF_LIVE, off by default (the function-flow thread's method, 2026-11-19): off, the flow is exactly main's. The swi clause is done ({unit:native/fnref-bios-reads}); passing a callee only what it reads is left to a later unit if this pays. Judged on C programs and games ({unit:native/c-bars}). Done when: unit tests; with the switch on fn_words_not_proven falls on Metroid or a C program, before and after in the evidence, no C or agb bar over on or off; Emerald's flow time and peak beside main's; on by default if it pays at near main's cost (then just holes-all before and after), else landed off with the reason; just check passes.

units.detail: The branch unit/native/fnref-unknown-addrs holds three units' work on crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs that isn't on main: frames and allocation sites as objects ({unit:native/fnref-heap-sites}), call-site context, off by default ({unit:native/fnref-context}), and RAM pointers followed ({unit:native/fnref-unknown-addrs}), with the metric fn_loads_read_everything (623 load sites on affine at the start, 3 now; barred in every table of lift-check.toml on the branch) and GBAA_FNREF_WATCH. june's answer (q/unknown-address-step-land-without, 2026-11-12): land it on that count, once native-irq-hold has its 16 typed heap accesses (ref_accesses) back, every other bar held, or raised with its cause named. On 2026-11-13 twelve bars are over (docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'Why the branch doesn't land'): native-irq-hold loses its two handlers' proven words (0x080001bc, 0x080001c0) and with them ref_accesses 16 to 0; ref_unexplained rises about 42 on native-bios-more, -bios-region, -dma and the spike because every call_fn set, all the address-taken functions, grows by the words now read; native-tasks has complete sets where main has none. Also unexplained: native-bios-calls' 571 loads that read everything. Judged on C programs and games ({unit:native/c-bars}, 2026-11-18; the owner's rule, {d:code-shape-lifter-work-is-judged-on-c-programs}): the branch lands only if it pays on the C programs of crates/codegen/lift-check.toml (c-fnptr, c-switch, c-chain, each by agbcc and by modern GCC; just lift-metrics) or a game's lift (Metroid or Nightmare, just lift, its metrics.toml): fn_words_not_proven, ref_unexplained or load_computed_unknown lower there, before and after in the evidence. If nothing pays on a C program or game, drop it instead (with the branch's three follow-ons).

units.title: Function flow: pointers into stack frames kept exact
units.detail: docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'Kinds of read switched off'. On affine, with GBAA_FNREF_OFF (unsound, measuring only; on the branch unit/native/fnref-unknown-addrs, as is all of this) the loads that read everything alone leave fn_words_not_proven at 55, reads through a pointer anywhere in an object alone leave it 55, and both off give 41: the two must be made exact together, and both are about stack frames. (1) The 3 loads left that read everything (affine 0x08000a24 to 0x08000a2c) go through a pointer into a caller's frame at or above the callee's entry sp, which Run::load_at gives up on (G::obj_up): follow it to the callers' frame objects through the sp each call passed. (2) A pointer into a frame moved by an index the run doesn't know becomes anywhere in the frame and reads every word of it: keep it in its stack slot (crates/codegen/src/native/frame.rs has the slots), and keep an array of pairs' fields apart (an offset known modulo the stride; core::fmt's argument arrays hold a value and a function each, affine 0x080036e4). Work on that branch (it has the object split, GBAA_FNREF_WATCH and GBAA_FNREF_OFF). Judged on C programs and games ({unit:native/c-bars}, 2026-11-18; the owner's rule, {d:code-shape-lifter-work-is-judged-on-c-programs}): affine's frame pointers found the problem, but the C programs of crates/codegen/lift-check.toml (c-fnptr, c-switch, c-chain, each by agbcc and by modern GCC; just lift-metrics) or a game's lift (Metroid or Nightmare, just lift, its metrics.toml) decides it (c-chain-agbcc passes pointers into its callers' frames: sp_accesses_callers_frame 4). Done when: unit tests for each; fn_loads_read_everything or fn_words_not_proven falls on a C program or a game (say in the evidence by how much and what holds the rest); on the agb programs neither rises (affine's 3 loads that read everything and its 55 words are measured, not a bar to reach). units.title: The IRQ wrapper's second half is discovered and lifted
units.detail: Found by the review of {unit:native/lift-psr-boot-irq}, 2026-11-13. The agbcc-shape IRQ wrapper (Metroid 0x08000104 and its IWRAM copy 0x03000c7c, Nightmare 0x03001030, Emerald 0x08000248, Rogue 0x0800025c, Imperium 0x08000264) calls its handler with 'add lr, pc, #0; bx r0' (Metroid 0x08000204). analysis::vsa::func::classify makes a bx a call only right after 'mov lr, pc', so this one is a jump, discovery has no code at its return site (0x0800020c), and the wrapper's second half (ldm, mrs cpsr, msr cpsr back to IRQ mode, IE and IME stores, msr spsr, bx lr) is in no lift. The lifter prints the call and then unreachable!("a call that never returns returned") (seen in Metroid's lift with the dispatcher stand-in dropped), so a lifted wrapper panics when its first handler returns. That is why the corpus counts 3 msr/mrs per wrapper where the code has 6, and why the games' IRQ-dispatcher stand-ins can't go yet (the reset stand-ins can). Do: have discovery take 'add lr, pc, #0' (lr = the address after the bx) as the call it is, so the return site is the same function's code and PsrFns prints its msr/mrs (if it comes out as its own function instead, PsrFns::place must cover it). It changes discovery for every program and the play build: run the scored checks (disc-*, jt-score) and the full just lift-check. Also add a standing check that runs printed PSR statements: today no lift-check program does (agb's wrapper keeps its stand-in in all 14; that unit's PR says how a hand run with --drop-standin 0x03000000 went). Smaller things from the same review: an sp write after a wrapper's mode switch is no longer a stack-switch hole in these functions (crates/codegen/src/native/frame.rs, the comment near line 451 is stale there); a wait or an ordinary function's I/O store while still in IRQ mode writes Game::sp with the IRQ-mode sp. Done when: Metroid and Nightmare lifted with their dispatcher stand-ins dropped print all six PSR statements of each wrapper and no unreachable! after the handler call; a native check that runs a lifted wrapper's whole path is in lift-check; lift-check, the scored checks and just check pass.

Metroid lifted with its dispatcher stand-ins (0x08000104, 0x03000c7c) dropped: 0 hard holes, six PSR statements in each wrapper, no unreachable! after the handler call, and it runs 600 of 600 frames; Nightmare with 0x03001030's dropped: six, none, and the same 11 entry-read hard holes as with its file as is. disc-pret (0.9997/0.9555, bars 0.9987/0.9349), disc-agb and jt-score (676/676, 610/617) pass and print as main's do. just check passes. units.title: Function flow gives a callee the r4-r11 it takes
units.detail: Since {unit:native/metroid-entry-reads} a direct call passes a callee the r4-r11 it reads at entry (Summary::takes; x_<key> with the caller's own), and so do the indirect calls a holes file's [[takes]] names. Two analyses made before that don't follow it. (1) The function-address flow (crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs, Edge::Call) gives a callee r0-r3 only, so a function pointer or a table's address that reaches a taker in r4-r11 is missing from its entry state, and a callee set built from it can be called complete when it isn't. (2) The frames (native/frame.rs) let a stack address in a taken register escape at a direct call, but not at a named pointer call: the summary's run refuses that call instead (only an address it sees as sp plus a constant). Metroid's one chain passes a constant that is only stored, so its lift is unaffected. Fix: give all registers at a direct call to a function with may_take() != 0 and at the named indirect calls, as Edge::Tail does; hand the frames the named sites. Done when: a test whose taker calls through a pointer it was passed in r8 gets that callee in its set; just lift-check passes.

units.title: Function flow: where a ROM table read by index ends
units.detail: From {unit:native/fnref-c-game-words} (docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'A C game', item 3). C lays tables of handlers back to back in ROM. A table read by a byte index is read 256 entries long, and a byte array whose address the run can't place is read as far as the value sets bound it, the index's width: 64 KB for a halfword. Run::object_end (crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs) doesn't stop between function words, and the bounded read (load_raw's hull path) doesn't stop at an object at all. On Metroid that is 77 words' first hole (0x08067f72, 0x08061aae), the 256-word reads behind the 429 words left in registers, and the width of the callee sets (18 sets of 210 callees, 73 on average). On Kirby Nightmare 64 KB reads of five byte arrays hold 1,401 of 4,054 held words (1,260 at 0x0801c6b8, the array at 0x08732ef0); on Emerald 1,209 of the 9,031 held when it stops. GBAA_FNREF_OFF=tables (unsound: it cuts at every object start) gives the upper bound: Metroid fn_words_not_proven 767 to 452 alone, 338 to 273 after bios. Find a sound end: a table's length from the compare that guards its index, from the next address a pool word holds that code indexes from, or from the entries' own shape. Done when: a rule that is sound (a unit test where a pointer into the middle of a table still reads to its end), Metroid's count and its callee sets' average size reported before and after and lower, the agb bars hold, just lift-check and just check pass.

record.evidence: Rule: a table starts where bounds start at a literal its function loads (stride kept by VSA); ends reads below unless a field. Tests incl. a_pointer_into_the_middle_of_a_table_still_reads_to_its_end (mutation-checked). Metroid fn_words_not_proven 338->274; complete callee sets avg 75.4->59.1, widest 210->167 (verifier reproduced 274/59.1/167). lift-metrics 0 over/under; just check and just lift-check pass after merging main. units.title: Function flow: old GCC's moves and compares with 0
units.detail: From {unit:native/fnref-c-game-words} (docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'A C game', item 4). Old GCC (every commercial C game) moves a low register with adds rd, rs, #0, and tests a callback with cmp r0, #0. The flow (crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs, Run::block's Op::Adc, AdcCarry, AdcOverflow arms) follows an add that sets flags only as a compare, so the move is arithmetic, and it counts the compare's carry as an ordered compare though it is constant. On Metroid 99 words' first hole is such a move (0x0800535a, 0x08001416, 0x080031f0) and 39 the carry of cmp r0, #0 in three callback setters (0x08000aea); on Emerald 473 at CreateTask's first instruction (0x080a8fb2). Sound rules, each small: x + 0 with carry 0 is x, its carry and overflow 0; x + !0 + 1 (cmp x, #0) always carries and never overflows; a value that may be a function or a number compared with 0 holes nothing (the Adc arm's bad test looks at the same operand's other numbers, not the other operand's); a flag set and never read before the function returns is no use (the N flag of cmp r0, #0). GBAA_FNREF_OFF=move does the first, flags switches all flag holes off (an upper bound). Alone they move nothing on Metroid (767 to 769, 767): the words meet the next hole, so this pays only with {unit:native/fnref-bios-reads} and the results half of {unit:native/fnref-live-registers}. Done when: each rule has a unit test, the two switches are gone or folded into the rules, Metroid's count is reported before and after, the agb bars hold, just lift-check and just check pass.

units.title: Function flow: struct tables read by one field
units.detail: From {unit:native/fnref-c-game-words} (docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'A C game', item 5). A ROM table of records read by index at one field (base + i * size + offset, a byte flag beside two function pointers) is read 'from here on' as every byte of the object, so the byte read gives the bytes of the records' function words, and their first use is arithmetic. On Metroid 66 words: 33 at 0x0805b4f8 (records of 24 bytes from 0x08345d00, the byte at +0, functions at +4 and +12), 15 at 0x080609b4 (records of 16), 18 at 0x08069dd8; they are still held with every GBAA_FNREF_OFF switch on. Keep the stride: a read through base plus an index scaled by a known size (the shift and add before the load, or the value sets' stride if they keep one) at a known offset reads only that field of each record (crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs, Tok::RomFrom and Run::rom_from). {unit:native/fnref-frame-pointers} has the same idea for arrays of pairs in a stack frame. Done when: a unit test with a table of (byte, function) records whose byte read leaves the functions proven, Metroid's count reported before and after, the agb bars hold, just lift-check and just check pass.

units.title: Function flow: the pile split by global, for C games
units.detail: From {unit:native/fnref-c-game-words} (docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'A C game', item 6). The flow keeps one pile for every store it can't place, and a load at a constant RAM address reads its cell and the pile. C keeps its state in globals: a callback stored in a struct through a pointer goes to the pile, and any byte loaded through a pointer then reads the bytes of every such callback. First road of 2,523 of Kirby Nightmare's 4,054 held words (733 at 0x08006162; with GBAA_FNREF_OFF=pile 1,599 are held) and 3,701 of the 9,031 Emerald holds when it stops; on Metroid 13, and at most 62 after {unit:native/fnref-bios-reads} (GBAA_FNREF_OFF=bios,pile: 338 to 276). {unit:native/fnref-heap-sites} splits by allocation site, which a C game doesn't have. The value-set analysis bounds 8,582 of Metroid's stores to one global and leaves 3,989 unbounded (store_ram_object, store_computed_unknown), so split the pile by those bounds, and stop a constant-address load reading the pile where every store that could reach its cell is bounded elsewhere. Measure on Nightmare (the flow settles there now: gbaa-recompile --summaries ROM --callee-sets, 31 to 35 minutes, 2.0 GB) with GBAA_FNREF_WATCH=roads. Do it after {unit:native/fnref-table-ends}: on Metroid the two reach the same words. Done when: a unit test with two globals whose stores stay apart, Nightmare's held words by pile reads reported before and after and lower, the agb bars hold, just lift-check and just check pass.

record.why: Measured, no gain: the value sets bound 246 of Metroid's 3,898 unplaced store sites and 76 spans on Nightmare, so splitting the pile by them left Metroid at 274 not proven and Nightmare's pile-read holds at 2,529 to 2,530 (commit c3954b9, reverted; docs/research/fnref-held-words.md). Nightmare's pile is stores at a RAM array's literal plus an index: {unit:native/fnref-ram-array-bases}.

units.title: A store or wait in IRQ mode banks sp, not Game::sp
units.detail: Left by {unit:native/lift-irq-wrapper-tail}, from the review of {unit:native/lift-psr-boot-irq}, 2026-11-13. An ordinary lifted function prints 'g.sp = r13' before a wait and before an I/O store that may set IME (crates/codegen/src/native.rs), and the prelude's helpers that take sp (intr_wait, cpu_set, cpu_fast_set, lz77: 'g.sp = sp') do the same, also when the reset or an IRQ wrapper calls them. Game::sp is system mode's banked sp (prelude banked_sp). If one runs while Game::cpsr's mode is IRQ (a lifted wrapper that calls something or makes a BIOS call before its msr to system mode, or one that never switches), it puts an IRQ-stack address in system mode's bank, and the wrapper's later msr_cpsr to system mode hands that back as sp. What the lifter prints in the reset and the wrappers themselves already banks by mode (bank_sp: I/O stores since {unit:native/lift-psr-boot-irq}; poll-loop waits and Halt since {unit:native/lift-irq-wrapper-tail}). No wrapper seen so far calls anything before its switch (Metroid 0x08000104, Nightmare 0x03001030, agb's InterruptHandler, agb/native-irq-wrapper's iw_main), so nothing is known to be wrong today; it was left out of that unit to keep its diff small, since it changes every lifted function's text. That unit's reviewer read the agb wrapper's stand-in (holes/*.toml, entry 0x03000000, which leaves Game::cpsr in IRQ mode while its handler runs on Game::sp) and found nothing reads either bank before irq_entry puts cpsr and the IRQ bank back (I is set, so dispatch returns early): printing bank_sp everywhere looks safe under it, to be proven by lift-check. Do: print bank_sp (or a prelude set_sp that picks the bank by mode) in every function and use it in the prelude's helpers. Done when: an agb program whose wrapper calls a function that stores to I/O before switching to system mode passes the native check, and just lift-check passes.

record.evidence: Every lifted function and the prelude's sp helpers now bank sp by mode (bank_sp). agb/native-irq-wrapper's iw_main acknowledges IF through iw_ack, an I/O store called in IRQ mode before its msr to system mode: lift-check --only native-irq-wrapper passes (600 frames, planted fault caught); with origin/main's codegen it fails at frame 33 (EWRAM 0x020000e0, the handler's noted sp). Full just lift-check passed before the merge of main; just check and lift-check --only native-irq-wrapper passed after it. Verifier subagent re-ran the program's check and the control and reviewed the diff: no bugs.

units.title: Nightmare's mixer reads through 0xe3a02004 at frame 5
units.detail: Left by {unit:native/nightmare-entry-reads}, 2026-11-13: the lift builds again and its first stop is 5 of 600 frames, no-memory, 'a byte load at 0xe3a02004', in f_030072e8 < f_030071df < f_03007151 < f_080cd8ad < f_080010cd < f_03001030 < f_080cfa6d < f_0800157d: m4a's IWRAM mixer, run from SoundMain inside the V-blank IRQ (the dispatcher's stand-in). The load is the sample loops' 'ldrsb r0, [r3], #1' (ROM source 0x080cdb1c on; the copy is 0x080cd930 to 0x03007150); r3 is the channel's current pointer, 'ldr r3, [r4, #40]' at 0x080cdac0, r4 the channel from the SoundInfo at [sp, #24]. 0xe3a02004 is no word of the ROM (it reads as ARM 'mov r2, #4'), so a channel's wave pointer, or sp under the mixer (the IRQ stand-in's stack), is wrong. Not the entry-read work: with the constant-branch rule off the lift's source differs only in the list-scan functions' modules. Find the cause against the interpreter (just first-stop, gbaa-interp), fix it or file what it needs. Done when: just lift ROM out/lift-kirby-nightmare --name kirby-nightmare runs past frame 5 and the next first stop is quoted; just check passes.

record.evidence: Cause: SoundMain's pushed frame (SoundInfo at sp+24) was promoted to Rust locals and never stored before its constant bx r3 into the IWRAM mixer (another context, reads unknown). Fix: crates/codegen/src/native/frame.rs, a tail call with a frame slot at or above its sp flushes the locals first; two unit tests. just lift ROM out/lift-kirby-nightmare --name kirby-nightmare now runs 147 of 600 frames; next first stop: no-function, a call or jump to 0x080cde1d (m4a command table), at guest pc 0x080ce035 in f_080cdf4d < f_080cd8ad < f_080010cd < f_03001030, filed as {unit:native/m4a-ply-table-entries}. just check passes (exit 0) before and after merging origin/main.

units.title: RAM-copy code only jumped into needs no [[takes]] entry
units.detail: Left by {unit:native/nightmare-entry-reads}, 2026-11-13. In a RAM copy's context the summaries take every function as one a pointer may call (saves/summary.rs, 'Code not in the ROM: any pointer may'), so each part of m4a's IWRAM mixer that reads r4-r11 as it came is a hard hole until the holes file names it: five '[[takes]] sites = []' entries in Nightmare's (SoundMainRAM and the four places it changes between Thumb and ARM by 'adr; bx'). Every m4a game with the mixer in IWRAM will need the same five by hand. Find a rule the lifter can apply itself (say: no ROM word holds the function's RAM key but a resolved constant jump's literal, and every way in that the lift prints is a jump), or decide the holes entries are the rule and write the m4a recipe in docs/research/native-holes.md. Done when: just lift on Nightmare reports 0 hard holes with those five entries removed, or the doc has the recipe and why no rule; just lift-check and just check pass.

record.evidence: Review fix made: jump_literals now collects every pc-relative load in each context; a literal is dropped from the pointer words only if no other load reads it. With the five sites=[] takes entries removed (copies in /tmp; Nightmare's copy also without the not-yet-landed [[stack]] table), gbaa-lift reports 0 hard holes on Nightmare and on Amazing Mirror. units.title: moonbeam's hard holes: 11 to 503 since calls pass registers
units.detail: Found by {unit:discovery/gcc-far-jump-bl} while measuring against main: 'just holes-all' gave moonbeam 11 hard holes at 20898d66 and 503 at f740b332, after {unit:native/metroid-entry-reads} merged (a call passes the r4-r11 its callee reads at entry). 500 functions now have 'reads r4-r11 at entry: rN, which X takes' and 220 are 'takes r4-r11 from its callers'. units.title: Function flow: a BIOS copy out of RAM carries no addresses
units.detail: Found by {unit:native/fnref-bios-reads}. The flow (crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs, Run::exit, Edge::Swi) follows CpuSet and CpuFastSet only from ROM: the source's words go to the pile. A copy whose source is RAM moves nothing, so a function's address stored at a constant RAM address (its cell) and copied elsewhere by the BIOS is not in what a load of the copy reads (that cell and the pile): the load gives no address, arithmetic on it is no hole, and the word stays proven though the lifted program computes with it. C games copy structs with CpuSet. Unsound, and older than that unit (which only made CpuFastSet's r3, a word it read, hold what a load from anywhere reads). The same for what the other calls read through a pointer and write back (the affine sets, MidiKey2Freq's wave header, the decompressors' bytes): arithmetic inside the BIOS on memory the flow never looks at. Done when: a BIOS copy from RAM, or from a source the run can't place, stores to the pile what a load of its source reads (its cells in range if the address and length are numbers, else every cell, and the pile), with a unit test (F stored at a cell, CpuSet to another, loaded there and added to: a hole); the other calls' memory reads are either modelled or written down as why not; Metroid's fn_words_not_proven and the agb bars are quoted before and after; just lift-check and just check pass.

record.evidence: Commit e22d768f (merged main: e22d768f). CpuSet/CpuFastSet out of RAM or an unplaceable source store to the pile what a load of the source reads (Run::bios_read); affine sets, decompressors, MidiKey2Freq hole what they read via r0 (bios_mem); the reason the other calls read no program memory is in the docs. New tests a_bios_copy_out_of_ram_carries_its_addresses and a_function_address_a_bios_call_computes_with_is_lost fail on the old flow and pass now (fnref: 54 passed). Metroid fn_words_not_proven 200 before and 200 after (604 of 804 proven). The 17 agb programs' metrics and generated code are unchanged. just check exit 0 after the merge. just lift-check passed with a temp toml raising only four lines bars that already fail at base f96c2c71 (filed as {unit:native/lift-lines-bars-stale}). An independent verifier (subagent a8feb25b) reviewed the code, reran the tests and the old-flow failure, and checked the numbers: no bugs.

units.title: longjmp: a return to another frame, counted nowhere
units.detail: Found by {unit:native/moonbeam-taker-chain}. moonbeam has newlib's setjmp (0x0803830d) and longjmp (0x08038325: ldm r0!, {r4-r12, sp, lr}; movs r0, r1; moveq r0, #1; bx lr). The summaries give longjmp only 'a jump to an unknown place' (soft) and the hole report counts nothing for it, so a native build has no hole there, yet a lifted longjmp can't return into setjmp's caller's frame: each function's r4-r11 and sp are its own Rust locals. setjmp itself now takes nothing (a context save). Done: say what the lift prints for longjmp's bx lr and what happens when it runs (a named stop, or a wrong return); if wrong or silent, the pair is a hard hole in the hole report and the lift (found by shape: a context restore, codegen::saves::summary's context_saves has the save's), or lifted as a stand-in pair (host unwinding to the setjmp call). Check on moonbeam whether a route reaches longjmp at all.

record.evidence: Lift of moonbeam: longjmp's ARM half f_08038328 (ldm r0!, {r4-r12, sp, lr}) was already a hard hole, 'CPU state: a stack switch', so compile_error! and the crate won't build: nothing runs it, no wrong return. The hole report counts it too (hard 7, CPU state 1). The hole now says 'a context restore (longjmp: a return into its save's caller's frame…)', test a_context_restore_is_a_named_hard_hole. Route: gbaa-interp --trace, 5400 idle frames: setjmp 9 times, longjmp and its error caller 0x0801421d never; returns census with the hole report's presses, 5400 frames: 0 calls abandoned (a longjmp would be one). just check passed after merging main.

Check: save in Metroid's native build, close the window, reopen, and the file is there.

units.title: A per-function check for any function in any game
units.detail: crates/native-fn-diff checks a native function against the interpreter from recorded entry states, but is wired to Emerald's ten (its NativeGame per game). Make it take a game and a function address, with a replacement from mods/<game>/ as the native side. Owner's view (2026-11-13): there is no proof, only tests, and tests bloat and cost CPU. So: store a seed, count and digest, not the states; make the reference the lifted function run natively (cheap, many inputs per second), with the interpreter as an occasional second reference; give each function a fixed budget and print its time. Done when: it runs on a Metroid function and on an agb one; a planted wrong replacement is caught, the differing byte named; the budget and time per function are printed; just check passes.

review.findings:
- Missing work: the card's What asks for 'the interpreter as an occasional second reference', but this branch leaves it out (docs/native-port-design.md:1700 says 'Not yet: the interpreter as a second reference (its own unit)'). The session moved it to a new unit, 'The per-function check's interpreter as second reference' ({unit:native/fn-check-interp}), about 36 minutes after claiming this one. That is well short of the ~3-hour split rule, and the card never asked for a split. Fix: either build it here (every Nth run, turn the native Game state at the checked call into a Machine, run the interpreter untimed from the key to the return, compare its end with the reference's, and print how many runs it also checked), or get the owner to accept the split and record that on this card.
- crates/codegen/src/native.rs:1840-1848: fn_check_main was inserted between library_standins' doc comment and the function itself. library_standins' doc ('`holes` with a stand-in for each library routine… unless the holes file has its own.') now runs into fn_check_main's doc, and library_standins (line 2011) has no doc at all. Fix: move fn_check_main (and its doc) above line 1840 or below library_standins, so each doc comment sits on its own function again.
- crates/codegen/src/native/prelude.rs:269-274: the same kind of misplacement. The new FN_CHECK, Accesses, ACCESSES and note/note_access block went between ram_at's doc comment ('The RAM offset of a guest EWRAM or IWRAM address (mirrors included).') and `fn ram_at` (line 315). That line now documents FN_CHECK, and ram_at has no doc. Fix: move the new block above line 269 so the doc stays on ram_at. lines_prelude in crates/codegen/lift-check.toml shouldn't change.
- crates/codegen/src/native/fn_check.rs (the driver's `main`, diff line ~1296): `std::process::ExitCode::from(report(None).max(1) as u8)` always exits 1. With GBAA_FN_CHECK_RUN_ON set, every budget can be spent and every function 'same', yet the run still prints 'the program stopped', and the report's 'fn-check: pass' line comes with exit status 1. Fix: when every budget was already spent (the same `all` test `call` uses), report with the frames run (`report(Some(..))`) and return its code unchanged; keep forcing 1 only when the program stopped short of the budgets.

units.title: LLM pilot: 20 Metroid functions as plain Rust
units.detail: Owner decision: LLM passes may alternate with the algorithmic lift. Claude rewrites 20 Metroid functions of mixed size and kind (leaf, loop, switch, struct access, calls, one storing a function pointer) as plain typed Rust, from the named lift. Each goes into mods/metroid/ as a stand-in (game-derived: never in the public repo), with its per-function check. The owner said there is no sound check, only tests: report, per function, whether it passes its budgeted check, what that check missed when the route check caught it, and the time and tokens it took. Done when: the 20 are written; each passes or its failure is written up; Metroid's route check passes with every passing one in place; findings in docs/research/llm-pilot.md with no game code quoted beyond a few instructions.

record.evidence: All 20 written (mods/metroid/llm-pilot.toml, private) and passing: just fn-check with all 20 keys --replace mods/metroid/llm-pilot.toml: 'fn-check: pass', every budget spent in 2996 frames, each digest as recorded (budgets 24-1000; DmaTransfer/BitFill at 24, as a variant's reference never returns: filed {unit:native/fn-check-run-cap}). Route: lift --layout guest with all 20 in place vs the --timing native play build, route-check --native units/metroid-native.toml --name metroid: pass, 2700 frames, 0 differences, audio same. Findings, times, tokens: docs/research/llm-pilot.md. just check passes after merging main. Branch also carries {unit:native/fn-check-any}'s unlanded branch.

notes.text: Session 2026-11-17 with june: 6 of 20 pass (list, budgets and findings in the private mods repo's llm-pilot.toml and llm-pilot-notes.md). Needs {unit:native/fn-check-any}'s branch (two more fixes on it). Run with --names $GBAA_DATA/names.

Per-function check: just fn-check ROM --name metroid --fn-check KEY --replace mods/metroid/fn-check.toml. Only functions the no-input run calls before its stop at frame 2998 can be checked; a stand-in's check = { seed, runs, digest } sets its budget.

units.title: C test programs built with agbcc and modern GCC
units.detail: Owner (2026-11-13): the agb programs are Rust compiled by LLVM, but every commercial game is C from agbcc (old GCC 2.95, pret's games, Metroid) or modern GCC, so lifter work tuned on agb fights shapes no game has (agb's allocator and heap, trait vtables, stack addresses passed everywhere). Add a C test-program template next to agb/template: a crt0, linker script and a tiny hardware header of our own (no game code, no libtonc or libgba unless its licence suits a public repo), built twice, with agbcc and with arm-none-eabi-gcc. Both are already in $GBAA_DATA via scripts/fetch-decomps.sh (src/agbcc-jzw, toolchains/arm-gnu-toolchain-15.2.rel1). Source only in git, ROMs built like the agb ones. Port three programs whose shapes the lifter's code-shape work needs: function pointers in a struct table and a callback list, a switch that compiles to a jump table, and a struct passed by pointer through a call chain. Each runs in the play build and joins just lift-check (0 differences, a planted fault caught). Done when: the template builds with both compilers in one recipe; the three programs, six ROMs, pass just lift-check; just lift-metrics reports them; docs/tools/commands.md has the entry; just check passes.

record.evidence: just c-tests builds c/template, c/fnptr, c/switch and c/chain with agbcc and with arm-none-eabi-gcc 15.2 in one recipe (8 ROMs, reproducible; each pair matches mGBA at frame 600). just lift-check --only the six c-* (after merging main): every metric within its bar; each 600 frames, 0 differences, packed layout the same, planted store caught (e.g. c-fnptr-gcc frame 63 IWRAM 0x03000070). just lift-metrics: 23 programs, 0 over. just check passed. The GCC fnptr lift first stopped calling an undiscovered leaf from its struct table: discovery's pointer scan now takes a struct's pointer pair (Emerald scores unchanged; decision recorded). Filed {unit:oracle/long-fill-frame-offset}.

units.title: Function flow: a large set takes every form at once
units.detail: Emerald's large entry sets (over 4,096 tokens) gain other forms (Lo, LoUp, Part, Cmp) of the same 5,157 origins a step a round, and 12k entries change each round. Metroid lift: 0x0807431c holes nothing now; its 77 words meet the next hole 0x0805aef6 (bit-test mask, filed {unit:native/fnref-bit-test-mask}), fn_words 604/200 unchanged vs main a25c1b0. lift-metrics: 0 over bars. just check passes after merging main.

units.title: Function flow: a store indexed from a RAM global stays in it
units.detail: From {unit:native/fnref-pile-globals}, which found the value sets bound too few stores to split the pile by (docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'The pile split by global, measured'). Nightmare's two largest pile roads, 763 words at 0x08006162 and 269 at 0x0800582a, are stores at a RAM literal plus an index loaded from memory: 0x030025f0 + 4i (a callback table) and 0x03002790 + 144i (records), whose index is a byte out of the pile, so the value sets give Top and the flow piles them; the loads that then read them are at 0x03002490 and 0x03002494, below both arrays. As table-ends does for ROM: a load or store whose address is a RAM literal the function loads plus an index the run can't place stays in the object from that literal to the next RAM literal the code indexes from (a start less than one entry past another is a field). Commit c3954b9 holds the spans this needs (Store::Bounded, read_bounded, reruns by span); it found bases only through the value sets. Settle first what C allows that this cuts short (a struct's array field indexed from the struct's address, &arr[k] indexed from). Measure on Nightmare (gbaa-recompile --summaries ROM --callee-sets, 9 to 11 min, under 4 GB) with GBAA_FNREF_WATCH=roads. Done when: a unit test with two RAM arrays whose indexed stores stay apart, Nightmare's held words by pile reads before (2,529 of 2,728 on main at 06479cc) and after and lower, Metroid's fn_words_not_proven not higher, the agb bars hold, just lift-check and just check pass.

record.why: Measured, no gain: stores at a RAM literal plus an index kept in their object (commit 0951b1b, reverted) left Nightmare at 2,715 held, 2,110 by pile reads, and Metroid at 200, with the flow 2 to 4 times as long. The index comes by a load through a global pointer the run can't place; follow-up {unit:native/fnref-ram-pointers}. docs/research/fnref-held-words.md.

units.title: Nightmare's flow lift: MPlayMain's r8-in-r0 hole

record.evidence: just check passed on 19188c7c (main + this branch), merged to main at 9b75ea91 (later changes are comments only)

units.title: The lift leaves out flag and register writes nobody reads
units.detail: From the LLM pilot (every one of its 20 Metroid rewrites drops them): stage A writes N, Z, C, V at every flag-setting instruction, prints add_with_carry once per result, and restores callee-saved registers (r4 = l8) before a return that passes only r0-r3. Liveness in the function proves them dead: flags are read only by a later condition or a fall into another function's extended entry; the summaries say what a call or return passes. Examples: UpdateInput 0x08000969, ResetFreeOam 0x08000a19, FixedInverse 0x08000a81. Metric: dead flag writes printed (bar 0 on the C rows). Check (code-shape work, judged on the C programs and Metroid): just lift-check passes with 0 differences on every program and every planted fault caught; the new metric barred on the C rows and in Metroid's private bars; Metroid's lift builds and runs 600 of 600 frames headless; just check passes. Pattern list: docs/research/llm-pilot.md.

units.title: A pop of the entry lr prints as a plain return
units.detail: From the LLM pilot (15 of its 20 rewrites): a function that pushes lr ends with if t & !3 == RET { return } else { call_fn(t) } on the popped word. The slot is a Rust local (frame-locals) written only from r14 at entry, and stage A's call passes RET there, so the call_fn arm is dead: print the return, with RET left in the register the pop went through. Examples: DMA2IntrCode 0x08003381, SoundPlay 0x08002a19, FixedInverse 0x08000a81, GetNoteDelay 0x080020d5, IntroHandler 0x0808117d. Metric: returns through call_fn on a proven entry lr (bar 0). Check (code-shape work, judged on the C programs and Metroid): just lift-check passes with 0 differences on every program and every planted fault caught; the new metric barred on the C rows and in Metroid's private bars; Metroid's lift builds and runs 600 of 600 frames headless; just check passes.
