units.title: Branch conditions print as comparisons and bit tests
units.detail: From the LLM pilot (12 of its 20 rewrites): cmp r1,#128; bgt is printed as add_with_carry and !(z | (n ^ v)); the rewrites say first > 127. units.title: A frame nothing points into leaves no sp or lr behind
units.detail: After {unit:native/frame-locals} a function whose slots are all Rust locals still prints the guest's frame: r13 = r13.wrapping_add(0xfffffffc) at entry and back at exit, the entry lr kept in a local (l4 = r14), and agbcc's pop {r0}; bx r0 leaving that lr in r0, so a void C function returns Ok(r0) as u32. Where no slot escapes and no callee is handed an address in the frame: print no sp arithmetic and no saved lr or saved callee-save locals, and don't return a register that holds only the popped lr (the summaries' results: a caller can't read it as a value). Say in the evidence how many functions still need sp passed down (a callee with an escaping frame) and what would remove it. Planted control as frame-locals' (the native check skips the guest stack). Example: c/switch tally (0x080004fd in out/lift-c-switch-agbcc), 20 lines of C lifted to 90. Metrics: functions printing sp arithmetic with no escaping slot (bar 0 on the C rows); functions returning the popped lr (bar 0). units.title: Accesses print as named fields, from the map's types
units.detail: Owner (2026-11-19): a pointer the lift can't place prints ld32(g, r4 + 0x54) where the C says kirby->hp; the whole-program proof ({unit:native/ref-heap}) leaves most such loads unknown (c-chain-agbcc: 59 unknown to 6 typed). Don't prove where a pointer points: take its type from the source map and carry it through the function. The mod view built the pieces: codegen::names loads [types], prototypes and [locals]; codegen::types gives Types::proto_of (r0-r3's parameter types), global_at, path and array_at (the field path of an access at a typed base plus a constant, bitfields and [values] names included); docs/mod-view-design.md gaps 6 and 7. It typed only within a block (435 of 2,701 accesses on Emerald's sample; the rest came in registers across blocks). Here: a function-wide flow of types over the lift's values, seeded by parameters (prototypes), typed globals' addresses, pointer fields loaded through a typed pointer, and a typed callee's return; a pointer plus a constant is a field, plus an index times the element size an element. A typed access prints through its type's fields (g.at(p).hp as heap.rs prints a Ref<T>'s), at the instruction's width; the bytes read are the same whatever the type says, so a wrong type can't change behaviour, and the native check must show that. Judge on Emerald (pret's map from just pret-names) and a C test program given a map; Kirby & the Amazing Mirror takes it once {unit:native/mirror-katam-names} gives its types. Metric: RAM accesses printed as a named field of all computed RAM accesses (a floor, barred, on the C row and Emerald). units.title: The names tool reads variables that change register
units.detail: From {unit:native/lift-typed-access}, 2026-11-19. pret-names reads a DWARF variable's location only where it is one register or stack slot for its whole scope, which is how agbcc writes them. Modern GCC moves a variable between registers and writes a location list (this register from here to here, then that one): on c-chain built by GCC 15 at -gdwarf-2, 4 of 34 locals get a location, against 28 of 30 for the agbcc build. Read location lists into [locals] as one row per range (the table already has from and to), and DWARF 5 units too if that is cheap (GCC 15's default; the C tests are built at -gdwarf-2 because the tool skips version 5 whole). No game lifted today needs it (the decomps we use build with agbcc); it is for the modern-GCC C tests and romhacks built with modern GCC (Rogue, Imperium). Done when: the dwarf report line counts c-chain-gcc's locals with a location at 25 or more of 34; the agbcc files come out byte-identical; c-chain-gcc's computed_unknown_unnamed bar is lowered; just check passes.

units.title: Function flow: RAM objects under GCC's section anchors
units.detail: From {unit:native/fnref-ram-pointers} (docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'RAM objects under GCC's anchors, and from the names, as landed'). Modern GCC addresses every global from one anchor (ldr r7, =anchor; ldr r0, [r7, #40]), so no literal starts an array and all of .bss was one object; and agbcc's arrays ran on over the globals after them to the next literal the code indexes from. Behind GBAA_FNREF_RAM: a global the names files name is an object, whole (the lift passes the names' data extents to the flow); and a sum that is a RAM literal, a constant and a scaled index is in the object at literal plus constant, taken at the instruction that makes it (GCC adds the index to the anchor first). Done when: unit tests; with GBAA_FNREF_HEAP and GBAA_FNREF_LIVE on fn_words_not_proven on c-heap-gcc and c-heap-agbcc lower than before this unit (6 each; values in the evidence), with GBAA_FNREF_RAM and GBAA_FNREF_LIVE no C program's higher than before, Metroid's not higher, no bar over with the RAM switch alone; off, the flow is main's; just check passes. What holds c-fnptr-gcc (a ROM table's field pointer kept across blocks) is {unit:native/fnref-table-fields-blocks}.

units.title: Function flow: a table field's stride across blocks
units.detail: From {unit:native/fnref-ram-anchors} (docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'RAM objects under GCC's anchors'). With GBAA_FNREF_RAM and GBAA_FNREF_LIVE on, c-fnptr built by modern GCC keeps 9 of 14 function words not proven where agbcc's has 0: its callee sets mix sObjOps' update and draw fields (5 callees where 3 and 2 are right), because GCC computes &sObjOps[kind] once and keeps it in a register across blocks, and the stride a ROM table's field pointer carries (Tok::RomStep, {unit:native/fnref-table-fields}) is found a block at a time (strides in crates/codegen/src/native/fnref.rs), so the load in the next block reads every word of the table. Carry the stride with the value (the token already has it once made: check where it is lost, at the block's edge or at the index's scaling in an earlier block) or follow the scale through registers across blocks as ram_indexed does. Done when: a unit test; fn_words_not_proven on c-fnptr-gcc lower with those switches (value in the evidence) or with none; no bar over off; Metroid's not higher; just check passes.

record.evidence: At the commit above, just check green (quack, 2026-11-21). Behind GBAA_FNREF_RAM; off, lift-metrics 0 over 0 under and Metroid's and Emerald's flow traces are main's line for line. Two causes, both modern GCC's shapes: the scaled index kept in r5 over a call (the card's), and add_obj's u8 kind scaled as it came (a word, so only its 4 was kept). Rule: each register's stride and whether it is under 2^16 followed through the function's blocks (steps_in), and r0-r3 under 2^16 at the entry of a function every direct call passes them so by what the caller itself makes (smalls; a loose function runs without). With GBAA_FNREF_RAM and GBAA_FNREF_LIVE: c-fnptr-gcc fn_words_not_proven 9 to 5 (9 of 14 proven), calls through sObjOps exact (update 3 callees where 5, draw 2 and 2), the two callback calls 5 callees where 9; every other C and agb program's row as before (lift-metrics 0 over, 17 under); Metroid 690 proven 124 not and its callee sets byte for byte as before; Emerald the same sets but the loose functions an incomplete call reaches 6,086 to 6,077, flow 964 s against 993 s off side by side on a busy machine. Unit tests: a_stride_kept_in_a_register_reaches_the_next_block, a_registers_stride_at_a_blocks_entry_is_what_every_way_in_gives, a_parameter_every_caller_passes_small_is_a_records_index. Review: a fresh subagent read the diff; one real bug (a loose caller's own parameter passed on counted as small), fixed with its test case; nothing else. The 5 left are the callbacks' words, held by the RAM object under GCC's anchor, not a ROM table. docs/research/fnref-held-words.md, 'A table field's stride across blocks and calls'.

units.title: Function flow: what Metroid's globals read from the pile
units.detail: From the function-flow thread, 2026-11-20 (docs/research/fnref-held-words.md). With GBAA_FNREF_LIVE on Metroid has 690 function words proven and 125 not: 33 never read, and of the 92 with a first road (GBAA_FNREF_WATCH=roads) 55 are held by a pile read at a constant address (34 at 0x08000b06, a callback loaded from its global and compared with 0: the load reads the pile too, which holds functions' bytes and halves), 13 used as an address by a RAM routine (0x030016ca), 13 stored outside RAM (8 at 0x0800323c), 9 arithmetic on the value itself. The RAM rules (GBAA_FNREF_RAM) don't move the 55: a load at a constant address still reads the pile. Tried and dropped: not reading back function addresses stored through an address the closed world says is not RAM (Metroid unchanged, 16 agb bars over by a line or two). Find what stores those words to the pile with the RAM rules on (GBAA_FNREF_WATCH=WORD on two of the 34) and whether a load at a constant address must read it. units.title: A direct call gives back the r4-r11 its callee changed
units.detail: From {unit:native/emerald-builds}: m4a's IWRAM mixer in the Pokemon games calls a helper by bl (0x03001e64, pret's SoundMainRAM_Unk1, Game Freak's compressed-sample path) that shares the mixer's registers: it changes r9 and returns, and the mixer stores r9 after (0x03001e28). Rule, the mirror of what a callee takes ({unit:native/metroid-entry-reads}): a function whose changed r4-r11 a direct caller reads gives them back (Summary::gives), the lift's call takes them into the caller's locals, and a function it tail-calls gives them too. units.title: A lifted game's cartridge clock answers (Emerald's RTC)
units.detail: june played Emerald's lift (2026-11-20, main 59263d82, target/recompiled/release/gbaa-native-emerald --scale 4) and got the game's message that the internal battery has run dry: the cartridge's real-time clock doesn't answer natively. The play build has it: runtime::gpio (the GPIO port at 0x080000C4-C9 and the Seiko S-3511 behind it, as mGBA's, by game code HAS_RTC), on the bus (crates/runtime/src/bus.rs). The lifted program's loads and stores don't reach it: the native hardware library has no GPIO port, so the game's clock probe reads the ROM's own bytes. Give the native side the same port (the lift's halfword stores and loads at those addresses going to runtime::gpio's model, the clock's time from the host as the play build takes it), with a test program or a route that reads the clock, and the native check comparing it against the play build. units.title: Emerald's lift stops on the naming screen (open-bus load)
units.detail: june played Emerald's lift (2026-11-20, main 59263d82) and it stopped at frame 7175 on the naming screen: 'a byte load at 0xe55ec003: no memory the program has there', functions 080e3c6d (SpriteCB_Underscore), pc 080e4a61 (GetTextEntryPosition). GetTextEntryPosition loads sNamingScreen (0x080e4a66), then its template pointer (0x080e4a6c), then the template's byte at +1 (0x080e4a6e). 0xe55ec002 is the BIOS region's value after an IRQ (runtime::bus::BIOS_LATCH_AFTER_IRQ), so sNamingScreen was NULL and the template pointer was read from the BIOS region: the last load is open bus. Two readings, not told apart yet: (a) the game's own use after free (the sprite callback running once after the screen freed sNamingScreen), which the hardware and the play build survive: then it is an [[open_bus]] at = 0x080e4a6e entry in mods/emerald/holes.toml, the table {unit:native/mirror-native-route} adds (not on main on 2026-11-20); (b) the lift left sNamingScreen NULL where the play build has it set: a lift bug to find. Tell them apart by running the play build (or the interpreter) to the same screen with the same presses and watching the address 0x080e4a6e loads from. Done when: the lift passes the naming screen as the play build does on a route that enters and leaves it (route-check --native, 0 differences); just check passes.

units.title: Loops counted to a variable bound print as for
units.detail: From the owner, 2026-11-20: loops as for is the first readability bar to move. Emerald's lift prints 353 loops as for and 4,030 as loop; pret's C has about 3,960 for loops (grep of pokeemerald src). {unit:native/lift-for-loops} proves only constant-start one-block loops; most C loops count to a parameter, a global or a field (HealPlayerParty: for (i = 0; i < gPlayerPartyCount; i++), lifted as 'l1: loop with r8 and a guard if before it). Wanted: (1) a guarded loop whose counter starts at a constant or a value and is compared to a bound that doesn't change in the body prints as for i in a..b (the guard before the loop is the proof the range isn't empty; narrow widths wrap as the C type does, so prove no wrap or keep loop); bodies of several blocks, with calls, with continue and break; down-counting as (a..b).rev(). (2) the counter is one variable named from DWARF (i, j), not a register beside a // dwarf note. Indexing by the counter is the next unit, {unit:native/lift-for-index}. A C test program in c/ with each loop shape (bound from a parameter, a global, a field; nested; down-counting; break inside; u8 counter). hw::spin on the back edge of a loop that calls functions is timing the play build shares: keep it as the body's last statement unless a proven counted loop can drop it in both builds with the route checks unchanged. Metrics: loops_for up, loops_not_for down; bar loops_not_for on the C rows and the games. Example: HealPlayerParty and CheckBagHasItem in out/lift-emerald. Check (code-shape work, judged on the C programs, Metroid and Emerald): just lift-check passes with 0 differences on every program and every planted fault caught; the metric barred on the C rows and in the private bars of Metroid and Emerald; both games build and run 600 of 600 frames headless; Emerald route check still 0 differences once {unit:native/emerald-native-route} is done; just check passes.

units.title: A stack array passed by address is a typed local
units.detail: From the owner, 2026-11-20 (the structural gaps between Emerald's lift and readable Rust). A local whose address is taken stays bytes on the guest stack: pret's u8 arg[4] in HealPlayerParty is st8(g, r6, v) with r13 passed to SetMonData. Emerald: sp_accesses_escaping_slot 14,563, bank_sp_calls 18,410, sp a parameter of nearly every function. docs/native-stage-b.md lists escaping slots as &mut as not filed; this files it. Wanted: an escaping slot whose address only reaches callees' pointer parameters (never RAM, never returned) is a Rust local of its type (DWARF's where the names files have it, else by access width: [u8; 4]) passed as a reference or a typed pointer to it; accesses are element or field accesses; a function with no slot left on the guest stack takes no sp and needs no bank_sp. A slot whose address reaches RAM keeps the guest stack ({unit:native/lift-frame-exact-narrow} narrows which those are: do that first or with it). Design first, a short section in docs/native-port-design.md: what a pointer to a host local is in a program whose other pointers are guest addresses (the native check compares RAM, and --shadow-locals is the control for a wrong escape). Replaces the decision that stage A keeps the guest stack as IWRAM bytes only where proven. Metrics: sp_accesses_escaping_slot and bank_sp_calls down, barred. Planted control as the stack units have (docs/native-stage-b.md, how every piece is checked, 3). Check (code-shape work, judged on the C programs, Metroid and Emerald): just lift-check passes with 0 differences on every program and every planted fault caught; the metric barred on the C rows and in the private bars of Metroid and Emerald; both games build and run 600 of 600 frames headless; Emerald route check still 0 differences once {unit:native/emerald-native-route} is done; just check passes.

units.detail: From the owner, 2026-11-20. Every pointer in the lift is a u32, and a typed access is built where it is used: g.get(Ref::<t::BagPocket>::new(r4.wrapping_add(0x2039dd8)).capacity()). Emerald: load_computed_unknown 43,661, store_computed_unknown 30,777, computed_unknown_unnamed 19,459, ref_unexplained 23,696, pointer_unexplained 4,829; Mirror: 62,289 Ref::<T>::new( ({unit:native/mirror-machine-count}, row 3). Wanted: a parameter, local, return value or field that holds a pointer has the type Ref<T> (or FnRef) in its declaration, so a use is p.capacity() or g.get(p.capacity()) with no ::new at the use, and pointer arithmetic is .idx(i) / .add(n) / a field path. Two sources, kept apart and counted apart: types the lift proves (value sets, {unit:native/ref-heap}'s tokens, what a callee does with its parameter, carried to callers and callees until they agree), which is what a game with no decomp gets; and types the names files give (prototypes, DWARF), the answer key that scores the first. A type changes no byte read, as now (--no-field-types is the control). Metrics: Ref::new at a use (new, barred), computed_unknown_unnamed down; and how many proven types agree with DWARF's on Emerald and Metroid, in the pret score ({unit:native/lift-pret-score}). Check (code-shape work, judged on the C programs, Metroid and Emerald): just lift-check passes with 0 differences on every program and every planted fault caught; the metric barred on the C rows and in the private bars of Metroid and Emerald; both games build and run 600 of 600 frames headless; Emerald route check still 0 differences once {unit:native/emerald-native-route} is done; just check passes.

units.title: Emerald's signatures print from pret's prototypes
units.detail: From the owner, 2026-11-20. A function whose summary has a hole (the analysis couldn't finish saying which of r0-r3 it reads and writes) takes and returns all four: CB2_InitTitleScreen(g, sp, a: [u32; 4]) -> Result<[u32; 4], Exit> for a void(void). Emerald: functions_summary_hole 3,912 of 15,215, regs_call_entries 3,622, callee_saves_unproven 3,878. The owner's call (2026-11-20, replacing this unit's first form, which kept prototypes as the answer key only): print from the prototypes; a game with no decomp will get its signatures from an agent or an algorithm later, and either writes the same names-file entries. So: (1) where the names files give a prototype, the function's parameters and result are the prototype's (count, names, and void / one value), hole or not, and callers pass and take back only those. (2) It must stay safe: where the summary proves the function reads a register the prototype doesn't give it, or a caller reads a result the prototype says isn't there (hand-written assembly, a wrong prototype), keep the summary's shape for that function and count it (new metric, listed by name in the report); the native check and fn-check are what catch a wrong prototype, with a planted wrong prototype as the control in lift-check. (3) A switch (--no-prototype-shapes) prints the summaries' shapes as today, and the table of holes by cause (a callee with a hole, an indirect call with an incomplete set, a jump by value, a fall into another function, a stand-in) goes in docs/research/ with how often the summaries agree with the prototypes where both speak: that is what an unworked game would get, scored in {unit:native/lift-pret-score}. Don't edit fnref.rs here. Metrics: regs_call_entries down, barred on the games; prototype shapes used and refused. Check (code-shape work, judged on the C programs, Metroid and Emerald): just lift-check passes with 0 differences on every program and every planted fault caught; the metric barred on the C rows and in the private bars of Metroid and Emerald; both games build and run 600 of 600 frames headless; Emerald route check still 0 differences once {unit:native/emerald-native-route} is done; just check passes.

units.title: A call takes back only the registers its caller reads
units.detail: From the owner, 2026-11-20. A shaped function returns every register it may change, so scratch registers a callee merely clobbered print as results: (r0, r2, r3) = GetMonData2(g, r13, v19, 0x3au32, r2)? where C has one return value, and r2 is passed in only because the callee's summary reads it on some path. docs/native-stage-b.md, known gaps, shapes return too much. Wanted: a function's results are the registers some caller reads after the call before writing them (whole program, with the callee sets for indirect calls; a function whose address is taken keeps what any indirect caller may read); a clobbered register nobody reads is not returned and the caller's copy is dead (AAPCS says r1-r3 are, but prove it per function, don't assume: hand-written assembly returns in r1-r3). The same for parameters only a dead path reads. Metrics: functions returning more than one register, and tuple-assigning calls (new, barred); score against pret's prototypes (void / one value) in {unit:native/lift-pret-score}. Check (code-shape work, judged on the C programs, Metroid and Emerald): just lift-check passes with 0 differences on every program and every planted fault caught; the metric barred on the C rows and in the private bars of Metroid and Emerald; both games build and run 600 of 600 frames headless; Emerald route check still 0 differences once {unit:native/emerald-native-route} is done; just check passes.

units.title: Lifted statements are indented by their nesting
units.detail: From the owner, 2026-11-20. In out/lift-emerald every statement sits at 16 spaces whatever its depth, pc(..) and loop/block openers at 4, and a call at 20: HealPlayerParty's two nested loops read flat. Print each statement at its block's depth (4 spaces a level), openers and closers with it, comments (// src/file.c:31, // dwarf r8: i) at the statement they belong to. No rustfmt run over the lift (850,000 lines; and a cut's three-way merge wants stable text): the printer does it. A printer test on a C program's lift: every line's leading spaces are 4 times its brace depth. A re-cut of an older cut still merges (git merge-file ignores nothing: say in docs/tools/commands.md that cuts made before this need --ours whitespace or a re-cut). Done when: the test passes, just lift-check and just check pass.

units.title: A for loop's counter indexes arrays as elements
units.detail: From the owner, 2026-11-20 (split from {unit:native/lift-for-bounds} so each is one sitting): array indexing by the loop variable where possible. After a loop prints as for i in a..b, what its body computes from the counter still prints as arithmetic: 0x64u32.wrapping_mul(r8).wrapping_add(0x20244ec) for &gPlayerParty[i], (r6 << 2) plus a loaded base for itemSlots[i], and agbcc's strength-reduced form where a second register steps by the element size beside the counter (r4 += 8 each pass, CheckBagHasItem). Wanted: an address or access that is a typed array's base plus the counter times its element size prints as the element (gPlayerParty[i], pocket.itemSlots[i].itemId), with {unit:native/lift-element-address}'s printing; a stepped pointer that is provably base + i * size on every pass is not a variable of its own but that element; where the array is a global of known length and the range is within it, no run-time index check is printed. The same address as before (--no-field-types is the control). Add the shapes to the loops C program of {unit:native/lift-for-bounds} (an array of structs, a field array through a pointer, two arrays by one counter, a stepped pointer). Metrics: named_index_accesses up; for loops whose body still multiplies or shifts the counter (new, barred on the C rows). Example: HealPlayerParty and CheckBagHasItem in out/lift-emerald. Check (code-shape work, judged on the C programs, Metroid and Emerald): just lift-check passes with 0 differences on every program and every planted fault caught; the metric barred on the C rows and in the private bars of Metroid and Emerald; both games build and run 600 of 600 frames headless; Emerald route check still 0 differences once {unit:native/emerald-native-route} is done; just check passes.
